name: 2002 TC302
periodText: About 56.1 hours suggested; no qualified phase
credit: Ortiz et al. (2020), combined occultation, photometry and astrometry, §3.
shapeMeaning: The 2018 occultation gives projected full axes 543.2 ±18 × 459.5 ±11 km. This smooth axisymmetric illustration assumes an unseen equatorial depth of 543.2 km and equator-on presentation; true 3D flattening is unresolved. It represents the primary outline, not the larger thermal system-size estimate.
orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF pole (RA 0°, Dec +90°), arbitrary prime meridian and rotational phase. A projected limb position angle is not an inertial pole measurement.
introduction: 2002 TC302 has a flattened outline measured during a stellar occultation. Its displayed depth is assumed; newer thermal analysis suggests a possible companion, which is not part of this primary-body model.
survey: Selected: peer-reviewed 2018 occultation ellipse with explicit assumed depth.
The 2021 event reported a preliminary equivalent diameter 500.3 ±2.5 km at EPSC 2022; it supports the size scale but does not replace the published complete ellipse.
A May 2026 thermal/occultation preprint supports a putative satellite; no confirmed companion shape or primary terrain is inferred from it.
